note: P-B-2018-74316-1198d12d, 2018 MCM B, Team 74316, 39 PDF pages of which 28 are printed and one (PDF p9) is blank apart from the shop watermark. 115 measured regions on 32 pages resolve to 56 figures, 35 grids and 24 exclusions. The exclusions are display mathematics (11 regions: the FPE/AIC/BIC criteria, the ECM derivation, the 226x226 transition matrix and its recursion, the M0 matrix, the fuzzy relation, the density and MIC definitions), repeated caption bands the detector boxed as separate artwork (6 regions of the Appendix-1 correlograms) and column slices of the two pasted panel tables (5 regions of Appendix 2 and Table2), which is the first paper in this batch where the same object is measured several times because the raster is wider than one region. The paper is a language-population forecast in three models: an autoregressive short-term model, a logistic long-term model and a Markov migration model, closed by an office-siting MINE model and a memo. Drawing is MATLAB throughout: 19 line plots, 17 plates, 14 surfaces, 4 dendrograms, 2 schematic maps, a bar chart and a scatter, with no colourbar, no heatmap and no contour in the paper, so the three-dimensional surfaces carry absolute value on height alone. Captions are almost all below their exhibit in the body and above it in the appendix, never state units, never name a variable, and 24 of 56 figures have no number at all - the appendix captions its plates with the Appendix heading. Numbering itself is broken twice over: Figure 12 and Figure 5 are each printed twice for different drawings, Figure 19 and 20 are printed out of order on p21, one figure prints no number, and the appendix re-uses 'Table2' with the colon glued to the word. Announcement is nearly absent: three grids are named in prose and no figure is, and the two grids that are re-read later are re-read after they printed. Two coverage gaps. First, half the paper's grids are pasted raster panels (Appendices 2, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16 and Table2) whose text layer keeps only the numbers the OCR could reach, so their cell counts are read from the printed rows and headers in the render, not from the text layer. Second, the detector counts one wide raster as three or four overlapping regions, which forces column slices into the exclusion list and makes the Appendix-6 unit-root dumps six separate grids where the paper prints one table of six language blocks.
rules: Numbering splits the paper in two: 32 of the 56 figures print 'Figure N:' and 24 print no number at all - the eight Appendix-1 correlograms, the Appendix-7 cells, the Appendix-8 plates and the Appendix-13 surfaces are captioned by their Appendix heading - and the numbered half repeats itself, Figure 12 on p13 and again on p14, Figure 5 on p6 and again on p30, plus one drawing captioned with the bare word 'Figure' and no number [caption.numbering].

Caption side follows kind and the appendix flips it: 41 of 56 figure captions print BELOW the artwork, and every one of the 15 that print above is an appendix plate whose caption is the Appendix heading sitting over the frame; grids split 25 below and 10 above, the above ones always being the pasted panel tables of Appendices 2, 9, 11 and 12 [caption.position].

Caption length is a caption, not a sentence: figure captions run 6 to 18 words and grid captions 4 to 14, no caption concludes anything, no caption states a condition or a parameter range, and not one uses a reporting voice [caption.words].

Units reach the caption exactly three times out of 91: once on the figure side - Figure 3's '(Unit: Millions)', carried by a single caption of the three it covers but governing all of them - and twice on the grid side, Table 2's full-width '（Unit: Millions）' and Table2's ten-unit note row, while the other 88 exhibits put the unit in an axis title, in a header cell, or nowhere at all [caption.units].

Neither side names its variables: no figure caption names a series or an axis, and no grid caption names a column. Parameters appear as bare values ('when (δ=-0.1, Nm=1000)', 'mu=3'), so a caption tells you what the object is and never what it is made of [caption.variable_count].

Drawing is three idioms plus three singletons: 19 line plots, 17 multi-panel plates, 12 MATLAB surface meshes, 4 dendrograms, 2 schematic lon/lat maps, 1 bar chart and 1 scatter schematic. There is no histogram, no box plot, no heatmap, no contour map and no pie anywhere in the paper, and the only chart a reader could mistake for a heatmap is the eight-class world map of Figure 15 [geometry.family].

Three dimensions are used for one thing only - a quantity spread over geography: 14 exhibits leave the plane, the 12 surface figures plus the 2 Appendix-13 plate figures whose four panels are each a mesh, and all 14 are surfaces over longitude and latitude in section 4.2 or Appendix 13. Every one is a MATLAB mesh: none isometric, none drawn as perspective bars, none a 3D scatter. No other section of the paper leaves the plane [geometry.three_d].

No figure in the paper carries a colourbar: 0 of 56. Height encodes the value and a single blue-to-red ramp is assumed, so nothing in the frame states what the top of the surface means in absolute terms [geometry.colorbar].

Keys sit inside the frame or not at all: 32 inside, 17 with no key, 3 above the frame in the p6 triple, 3 outside right and 1 outside left. The four that put the key outside the plot area are the only cases where the reader's eye has to leave the marks, and two of those keys are cut by the measured region [geometry.legend].

Panel grammar has four states and no others: a single frame (39 figures), a 1x3 strip for a correlogram with its statistics grid (10), a 1x4 or 2x2 block for a parameter sweep (4), and a 1x2 before/after pair (3). Panel identity is always inline text - mu=3, 2017, 'Portuguese' - never a panel letter and never a second caption [geometry.panel_count].

Ruling has three registers and one outlier: 23 grids use booktabs (horizontal rules only, no box), 11 are fully boxed cell by cell, and exactly one grid is ruled vertically only - the Appendix-12 coordinate blocks, a line between every column and none between the rows. No grid is unruled, none is zebra-striped and none carries a diagonal header [table.rule_style].

Merged cells appear in 6 of 35 grids and always for one of two jobs - a spanner over grouped columns (Table 2's language families, Table 4's three information criteria, Appendix 3's three trend specifications) or a label merged down the rows it repeats (Table 13's symbols, the two 54-row panel tables, Appendix 9's continent headers) - never for emphasis alone [table.merged_cells].

Header depth is one row in 32 of 35 grids; the three that need two are Table 2, Table 4 and Appendix 3's critical-value block, which are exactly the three grids that spanner their own columns [table.header_rows].

Numbers are decimal-aligned in 23 of 35 grids. The 12 exceptions are the grids whose cells are integers rather than measurements (the migrant-count matrix of Appendix 9, the population block of Appendix 11, the Appendix-15 score card, the closing evaluation vector) and the grids whose cells are words ('No Exist', 'Yes', 'Unit Root?', the coordinate blocks of Appendix 12), which are centred instead [table.decimal_aligned].

A unit reaches a header cell three times only - Table 12's '(50 Years)' inside the column names, the two panel tables' '(per capita)' - and everywhere else the header names the quantity and leaves the unit to the note row or to nothing [table.units_in_header].

Every grid runs the full text measure: 35 of 35 are full-width. Nothing in this paper is typeset for a narrow column, so even the two-column symbol grids of Tables 1 and 13 spread across the whole page [table.width].

The appendix is where the exhibits are: 41 of the 91 rows sit under the Appendix heading, against 30 in model sections, 9 in 'other', 6 in sensitivity, 2 symbol grids, 2 solution grids and 1 in the memo's Results. A reader who stops at the body loses half the drawings [place.section_kind].
No exhibit owns a page: 0 of 91 is alone on its page, and the vertical band splits 29 top, 43 middle, 19 bottom, so every exhibit is wedged between prose and the next exhibit [place.solo_page].

Announcement is almost absent: 3 of 91 exhibits are named in prose at all, all three grids, and two of them are named AFTER they printed - Table 2 and Table 5 are re-read on p10, four and two pages on. Not one figure is cited by number anywhere in the body [mention.lead_pages].

Citation vocabulary is one construction: the single prose citation of an exhibit is as-shown-in ('the top 6 countries are shown in the table 16'), lowercased, and every other exhibit is reached only through 'as following', 'the graphs' or 'the table' [mention.lead_pattern].

Reading sentences are stock: 'The graph shows that ...' and 'From the results ...' repeat verbatim across sections and across exhibit kinds, so what follows a figure is a template, not an observation [mention.trail_sentence].

Two labels are duplicated and one is missing, and none of it is an extraction artefact: the paper prints two different Figure 12s, two different Figure 5s and one unnumbered figure, and the appendix prints a 'Table2' that re-uses a body number with its colon glued to the word [caption.verbatim].
